lessons.title: May for Possibility
lessons.content: 'May' is used to express possibility. It suggests something is possible but not certain. The structure is Subject + may + V1.

details.explanation: 'May' is used when something is possible but not certain.
details.burmese: သူ အိမ်မှာ ရှိနိုင်တယ်။

details.explanation: 'May' is used for possible future events like weather.
details.burmese: မနက်ဖန် မိုးရွာနိုင်တယ်။

lessons.title: May for Permission
lessons.content: 'May' is used to express permission. 'May not' is used to deny permission. This is a formal way to ask for or give permission.

details.explanation: 'May' is used to politely ask for permission.
details.example: May I come in, Sir? Yes, you may.
details.burmese: ဆရာ၊ ဝင်လို့ ရမလား။ ရတယ်၊ ဝင်လို့ရတယ်။

details.explanation: 'May not' is used to deny permission.
details.example: May I go home now? No, you may not.
details.burmese: အခု အိမ်ပြန်လို့ ရမလား။ မရဘူး၊ ပြန်လို့ မရဘူး။

lessons.title: May for Wishes
lessons.content: 'May' is used to express wishes or hopes. This is often used in formal or literary expressions.

details.explanation: 'May' is used to express blessings and good wishes.
details.burmese: ဘုရားသခင် ကောင်းကြီးပေးပါစေ!

details.explanation: 'May' is used to wish peace for someone.
details.example: May his soul rest in peace!

details.explanation: 'May' is used to wish success in contributing.
details.burmese: လူမှုအသိုင်းအဝိုင်းအတွက် ပါဝင်ကူညီနိုင်ပါစေ!

lessons.title: Might as Past Tense of May (Reported Speech)
lessons.content: 'Might' is the past tense of 'may' in indirect or reported speech. When we report what someone said, 'may' changes to 'might'.

details.example: He said, "I may go to school." → He said that he might go to school.

details.explanation: The same rule applies for writing activities.
details.example: John said, "I may write a letter." → John said that he might write a letter.

lessons.title: Might for Less Possibility
lessons.content: 'Might' shows less possibility than 'may'. May suggests about 50% possibility, while might suggests about 30% possibility.

details.explanation: 'May' suggests a higher chance of something happening (about 50%).
'Might' suggests a lower chance of something happening (about 30%).
